scope.flow: reward distribution via the distributeRewards() yield calculation loop

statements.text: The contract's token balance (balance_) is below depositPool.lastUnderlyingBalance at the time distributeRewards() is called.
A balance-decreasing scenario occurs, such as an AAVE slashing event, token transfer/holding fee, deflationary burn, forced liquidation, protocol upgrade affecting balances, or precision loss.
The yield calculation subtracts lastUnderlyingBalance from balance_ without first checking that balance_ is greater than or equal to lastUnderlyingBalance.
When balance_ is below lastUnderlyingBalance, the transaction reverts with panic code 0x11 (arithmetic underflow).

Calls to distributeRewards() fail and the condition persists because lastUnderlyingBalance is never updated, so users cannot receive earned rewards and reward distribution halts until manual intervention.

Inferred: distributeRewards() should distribute accumulated rewards to recipients without reverting when the contract token balance has fallen below the last recorded underlying balance at the yield-calculation checkpoint.

ambiguities: The caller of distributeRewards() and any required authorization are not specified; it is unknown whether any external user or only administrators can invoke it.
All balance-decrease triggers are described as possible scenarios ('can be triggered'), not as an incident that actually occurred in a transaction.
Whether an attacker can deliberately induce the balance decrease is not established; the report states the condition 'can occur naturally without attacker action'.
The persistence claim assumes lastUnderlyingBalance is only updated within distributeRewards() and that reverts prevent all updates, but alternative update paths are not discussed.
